summary: Port the NInfer single-GPU inference engine (sm_89 lineage) to the NVIDIA L20.

base.note: The branch tip is tracked by default. No commit is pinned: provenance (the SHA the port was applied to) is recorded in build-info.json after every build, never consumed as an input.

target.note: Documentation values only. The build queries the live device (device_sm_count() / nvidia-smi) at runtime; none of these numbers are hard-coded into the compiled engine.

os.note: 22.04 cannot satisfy the FFmpeg/libcurl version floors below; 24.04 satisfies them from its own repositories.

changes.description: Define the architecture identity macro (NINFER_SM86 / NINFER_SM89) at directory scope from CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES, so every target agrees on the architecture and Ada is no longer compiled under the Ampere name.

transforms.replace:
project(ninfer LANGUAGES C CXX CUDA)

# --- Architecture identity ---------------------------------------------------
# Ada (sm_89) and Ampere (sm_86) share one compatibility kernel organization, and Ada has no
# Programmatic Dependent Launch, so the compatibility switches must accept either symbol. Ada is
# nevertheless a distinct target: the declared device is the NVIDIA L20 (AD102, 92 SMs). Defined at
# directory scope so ninfer_core and ninfer_ops cannot disagree about the architecture.
if(CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES STREQUAL "86")
  add_compile_definitions(NINFER_SM86=1)
elseif(CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES STREQUAL "89")
  add_compile_definitions(NINFER_SM89=1)
endif()

changes.description: Remove the hard-coded NINFER_SM86=1 target definition from src/CMakeLists.txt (it labelled the sm_89 build Ampere). The NVFP4 source filtering the definition guarded is kept; the identity now comes from the top-level directory-scope definition.

transforms.replace:
# The architecture identity macro is defined once at directory scope in the top-level
  # CMakeLists.txt, where the architecture is validated. Do not re-derive it here: doing so is what
  # labelled the sm_89 build NINFER_SM86.

changes.description: Declare device_sm_count(): the runtime streaming-multiprocessor count of the device this process runs on, queried once and cached. Launch geometry that fills one resident wave reads the count from here instead of transcribing a per-part literal.
Implement device_sm_count() with a one-shot cached cudaGetDeviceProperties query.

Size the GDN chunked-output resident wave from the runtime SM count instead of the hard-coded RTX 5090 literal (170 SMs * 4 = 680 CTAs). This kernel runs on every GDN layer; 49 of the 65 Qwen3.8-27B layers are GDN. The wrong target also mis-selects the MULTI_JOB kernel specialisation.

Derive the sparse-MoE prefill grid cap from the runtime SM count instead of the hard-coded RTX 5090 literal. Only the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B target routes through this kernel (Qwen3.8-27B is dense), patched so the tree carries no per-part SM literal. The grid strides its work list, so any cap is correct; the runtime value keeps a narrower device from being over-subscribed.

Correct the cooperative-residency constant the launch clamp actually reads: for Bf16Gdn27Geometry only split-8 (256 threads, 65 regs) fits two CTAs per SM; split-4/split-2 (512 threads, 74 regs) fit one. Returning 2 for every split overstated the device-wide budget and the driver rejected the launch with cudaErrorCooperativeLaunchTooLarge on a part with fewer SMs than the RTX 4090 (the L20's one real crash).

Every NINFER_SM86 preprocessor conditional in the tree also accepts NINFER_SM89. Mechanical and behaviour-preserving: the branch Ada already took under the Ampere name is the compatibility branch. The file set is derived at runtime from the tree, so files added, renamed or rewritten by upstream are picked up automatically. No file list and no line numbers are stored here.
